sections.title: Prospectus Summary
text: The following summary is qualified in its entirety by, and should be read in conjunction with, the more detailed information and financial statements included elsewhere in this prospectus. In addition to this summary, we urge you to read the entire prospectus carefully, especially the risks of investing in our common stock, discussed under “Risk Factors,” before deciding whether to buy our common stock.

We are a Texas-headquartered, digital infrastructure company focused on providing secure and efficient hosting and O&M services for Bitcoin mining operations. Leveraging our purpose-built and fully operated mining sites located in Wheeler, Texas, and Dumas, Texas, as well as a contracted mining site in Marion, Indiana, we have developed operational processes and service capabilities that have supported stable operations and consistent service delivery for our customers. Through ongoing monitoring, established infrastructure, and third-party service arrangements, we seek to provide reliable power availability, network connectivity, and comprehensive facility management under normal operating conditions, with the objective of supporting mining machine uptime and computational performance.

Our hosting services encompass the entire lifecycle of Bitcoin mining operations, including mining machine deployment, preventive maintenance, system optimization, power management, and performance analytics, offering customers a fully integrated, one-stop infrastructure solution. sections.title: Risk Factors
text: An investment in our common stock involves a high degree of risk. Before deciding whether to invest in our common stock, you should consider carefully the risks described below, together with all of the other information set forth in this prospectus, including the section titled “Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations” and our consolidated financial statements and related notes included elsewhere in this prospectus. If any of these risks actually occurs, our business, financial condition, results of operations, or cash flow could be materially and adversely affected, which could cause the trading price of our common stock to decline, resulting in a loss of all or part of your investment. The risks described below and discussed in other parts of this prospectus are not the only ones that we face. Additional risks not presently known to us or that we currently deem immaterial may also affect our business. You should only consider investing in our common stock if you can bear the risk of loss of your entire investment.

Our business is capital-intensive and closely tied to the economics of digital assets, particularly Bitcoin. Demand for our hosting, O&M, and consulting services depends in part on the profitability and financial condition of our customers’ digital asset mining operations, which are subject to significant volatility. Although our planned business operations, including our strategy to develop a comprehensive consulting and infrastructure platform focused on digital assets, may alter the timing or mix of demand compared to our current operations, these services remain closely linked to the digital asset mining industry and are therefore subject to substantially similar industry, market, and regulatory risks.

sections.title: Use of Proceeds
text: Based upon an assumed initial public offering price of $7.00 per share of our common stock, we estimate that we will receive net proceeds from this offering, after deducting the estimated underwriting discounts and the estimated offering expenses payable by us, of approximately $26,954,565 if the underwriters do not exercise their over-allotment option, and $31,162,065 if the underwriters exercise their over-allotment option in full.
We currently intend to use the net proceeds we receive from this offering as follows:

• approximately 10%, or $2.69 million assuming no over-allotment option is exercised, or $3.12 million if the over-allotment option is exercised in full, for research and development of next-generation high-performance computing and energy-efficient technologies, including AI algorithm optimization and clean energy–powered mining management systems;

• approximately 40%, or $10.78 million assuming no over-allotment option is exercised, or $12.46 million if the over-allotment option is exercised in full, for strategic acquisitions and investments aimed at integrating potential target companies specializing in blockchain infrastructure, artificial intelligence, or energy innovation technologies (other than the Tripartite Agreement for AI Factory Development with Aleria and Ricloud AI Inc. in connection with the proposed development of an AI data center project in Wheeler, Texas, which does not obligate the parties to consummate any definitive transaction, see “Business—Growth Strategies,” we have not yet identified nor entered into preliminary negotiations with any specific acquisition target and do not have any agreements for acquisitions or investments as of the date of this prospectus); any issuance of our securities in connection with such acquisitions or investments during the applicable lock-up period will be subject to the applicable restrictions and exceptions set forth in the underwriting agreement described under “Underwriting—Lock-up Agreements”;

• approximately 30%, or $8.09 million assuming no over-allotment option is exercised, or $9.35 million if the over-allotment option is exercised in full, for global market expansion and brand development, encompassing marketing initiatives, customer engagement, and channel development across the North American and Asian markets;

• approximately 15%, or $4.04 million assuming no over-allotment option is exercised, or $4.67 million if the over-allotment option is exercised in full, for new mining operations and infrastructure development, including land acquisition, power integration, equipment procurement, and on-site operational expenditures; and

• approximately 5%, or $1.35 million assuming no over-allotment option is exercised, or $1.56 million if the over-allotment option is exercised in full, for general corporate purposes and working capital requirements.

The foregoing represents our current intentions based upon our present plans and business conditions to use and allocate the net proceeds of this offering. Our management, however, will have significant flexibility and discretion to apply the net proceeds of this offering. If an unforeseen event occurs or business conditions change, we may use the proceeds of this offering differently than as described in this prospectus. To the extent that the net proceeds we receive from this offering are not immediately used for the above purposes, we may invest our net proceeds in short-term, interest-bearing bank deposits or debt instruments.

A $1.00 increase (decrease) in the assumed initial public offering price of $7.00 per share would increase (decrease) the amount of proceeds to us from this offering available by approximately $4.01 million, assuming the number of shares offered by us, as set forth on the cover page of this prospectus, remains the same, and after deducting the estimated underwriting discounts and the estimated offering expenses payable by us. An increase (decrease) of 1,000,000 shares from the expected number of shares to be sold by us in this offering, assuming no change in the assumed initial public offering price per share, would increase (decrease) the amount of proceeds to us from this offering available by approximately $6.55 million.

sections.title: Dividend Policy
text: For the fiscal year ended July 31, 2025, we paid cash dividends of $100,000 on our common stock. For the nine months ended April 30, 2026, we did not pay any cash dividends on our common stock, and our board of directors intends to continue a policy of retaining earnings, if any, for use in our operations, though we may change this policy in the future. We are organized under the Texas Business Organizations Code, which prohibits the payment of a dividend if the corporation’s capital is less than the capital represented by all outstanding share having a preference upon the distribution of assets. Any determination by our board of directors to pay dividends in the future to stockholders will be dependent upon our operational results, financial condition, capital requirements, business projections, general business conditions, statutory and regulatory restrictions, and any other factors deemed appropriate by our board of directors.

sections.title: Dilution
text: If you invest in our common stock, your ownership interest will be diluted to the extent of the difference between the initial public offering price per share of our common stock in this offering and the net tangible book value per share of common stock upon completion of this offering. Dilution results from the fact that the initial public offering price per share is substantially in excess of the net tangible book value per share attributable to the existing stockholders for our presently outstanding shares of common stock.

Our net tangible book value as of April 30, 2026 was $2,415,988, or $0.06 per share of common stock. Net tangible book value represents the amount of our total consolidated tangible assets, less the amount of our total consolidated liabilities. Dilution is determined by subtracting the net tangible book value per share of common stock (as adjusted for the offering) from the initial public offering price per share and after deducting the estimated underwriting discounts and the estimated offering expenses payable by us.

After giving effect to our sale of 4,285,715 shares of common stock offered in this offering based on the initial public offering price of $7.00 per share, after deduction of the estimated underwriting discounts and the estimated offering expenses payable by us, our as-adjusted net tangible book value as of April 30, 2026, would have been $29,735,013, or $0.69 per outstanding share of common stock. This represents an immediate increase in net tangible book value of $0.63 per share of common stock to the existing stockholders, and an immediate dilution in net tangible book value of $6.31 per share to investors purchasing the common stock in this offering. The as-adjusted information discussed above is illustrative only and may change based on the actual initial public offering price and other terms of this offering.

The following is a brief biography of each of our executive officers, directors, and director appointees:

Mr. Chang Yao has served as our director since October 2025 and Co-Chief Executive Officer since May 2026. Mr. Yao served as our Chief Executive Officer between November 2025 and April 2026. Mr. Yao devoted most of his time to the management and operations of our Company, with a primary focus on strategic planning and business development. He also provides limited strategic guidance to other entities, which does not affect the performance of his duties within our Company. Mr. Yao founded Falcon Innovative Technologies LLC in November 2024, a company that provides AI-supported body camera solutions for government and law enforcement agencies, and has served as its Chief Executive Officer, where he leads the company’s AI algorithm development, business strategy, and government project partnerships. Since 2019, Mr. Yao has served as an Assistant Researcher at University of California, Los Angeles, where he designs and conducts experiments, researches advanced communication methods, and manages laboratory operations. From November 2022 to November 2024, he served as Chief Executive Officer at TY & Rex INC, an automotive export and brokerage company specializing in exotic and luxury vehicles, where he was responsible for the company’s overseas business operations. sections.title: Description of Capital Stock
text: The following description of our capital stock is a summary only and not meant to be complete but is subject to and qualified in its entirety by our Certificate of Formation and Bylaws, and by the provisions of the applicable Texas law. Reference is made to our Certificate of Formation, copies of which are filed as an exhibit to the registration statement of which this prospectus is a part.

Under our Certificate of Formation, we are authorized to issue up to 500,000,000 shares of common stock with par value $0.0001 per share. As of the date of this prospectus, there are 38,800,000 shares of common stock issued and outstanding. All of the outstanding shares of common stock are validly issued, fully paid, and non-assessable.
• Governing Documents. Holders of shares of our common stock have the rights set forth in our Certificate of Formation and Bylaws, and applicable Texas law;

• Dividend Rights and Distributions. The holders of our common stock are entitled to share equally in dividends, if any, as may be declared from time to time by the board of directors out of funds legally available for that purpose;
• Conversion Rights. Our common stock is not convertible into any other shares of our capital stock;
• Voting Rights. Each holder of our common stock is entitled to one vote per share on all matters to be voted upon by stockholders. Holders of our common stock do not have cumulative voting rights.
• Redemption. We have no obligation or right to redeem our common stock; and

• Assets Upon Dissolution. Our common stock ranks junior with respect to dividend rights and rights upon our liquidation, dissolution, or winding up to all other securities and indebtedness. In the event of liquidation, dissolution, or winding up, the holders of our common stock would be entitled to share equally on a per share basis, after payment or provision for payment of all our debts and liabilities, all of our remaining assets available for distribution.

In general, under Rule 144 as currently in effect, beginning 90 days after the date of this prospectus, a person who is not deemed to have been our affiliate at any time during the three months preceding a sale and who has beneficially owned restricted securities within the meaning of Rule 144 for more than six months would be entitled to sell an unlimited number of those securities, subject only to the availability of current public information about us. A non-affiliate who has beneficially owned restricted securities for at least one year from the later of the date these shares of common stock were acquired from us or from our affiliate would be entitled to freely sell those shares.

sections.title: Report of Independent Registered Public Accounting Firm (PCAOB ID Number: 6413)
text: We have audited the accompanying consolidated balance sheets of Bitari Inc. and its subsidiary (the Company) as of July 31, 2025 and 2024, and the related consolidated statements of operations income, comprehensive income, stockholders’ equity, and cash flows for each of the years in the two-year period ended July 31, 2025, and the related notes (collectively referred to as the consolidated financial statements). In our opinion, the consolidated financial statements present fairly, in all material respects, the financial position of the Company as of July 31, 2025 and 2024, and the results of its operations and its cash flows for each of the years in the two-year period ended July 31, 2025, in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America.

These consolidated financial statements are the responsibility of the Company’s management. Our responsibility is to express an opinion on the Company’s consolidated financial statements based on our audits. We are a public accounting firm registered with the PCAOB and are required to be independent with respect to the Company in accordance with the U.S. federal securities laws and the applicable rules and regulations of the Securities and Exchange Commission and the PCAOB.

We conducted our audits in accordance with the standards of the PCAOB. Those standards require that we plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the consolidated financial statements are free of material misstatement, whether due to error or fraud. summary: Risks related to blockchain, digital assets, and bitcoin mining may adversely affect our current and planned business operations (see page 6 of this prospectus);

Our business is capital intensive, and failure to obtain the necessary capital when needed may force us to delay, limit, or terminate our expansion efforts or other operations, which could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, and results of operations (see page 6 of this prospectus);

We are highly dependent on a limited number of electricity suppliers, and any disruption in their power supply could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, and results of operations (see page 7 of this prospectus);

Our use rights over our current and future hosting sites depend on land lease, easement, or other contracts, and any dispute or termination could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, and results of operations (see page 7 of this prospectus);

If future prices of Bitcoin are not sufficiently high, our business, results of operations, and financial condition could be materially and adversely affected, which may have a negative impact on the trading price of our securities (see page 7 of this prospectus);

Increases in power costs, or our inability to efficiently support digital asset mining activities, could impair our ability to attract customers, harm our growth prospects, and have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, and results of operations (see page 7 of this prospectus);

Governments and government regulators may potentially restrict the ability of electricity suppliers to provide electricity to hosting and transaction processing operations, which could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, and results of operations (see page 7 of this prospectus);

If our third-party O&M service provider fails to perform properly or meet our performance standards, our business, financial condition and results of operations could be materially and adversely affected (see page 8 of this prospectus);
Changes in tariffs or import restrictions could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, and results of operations (see page 8 of this prospectus);

Our revenue comes from a small number of customers, and the loss of, or significant decrease in business from, a number of these customers or our failure to continually attract new customers could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, and results of operations (see page 8 of this prospectus);

If we do not accurately predict our hosting facility requirements, it could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, and results of operations (see page 9 of this prospectus);
Power outages in our hosting site could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, and results of operations (see page 9 of this prospectus);
Changes in blockchain validation protocols could reduce demand for our hosting services (see page 9 of this prospectus);

Our success is dependent on the ability of our management team and our ability to attract, develop, motivate, and retain other well-qualified employees, which may be more difficult, costly, or time-consuming than expected (see page 10 of this prospectus); and

We may not be able to successfully develop and operate new data center infrastructure, which could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, and results of operations (see page 11 of this prospectus).

Changes in U.S. regulatory interpretation relating to digital asset mining and hosting could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, and results of operations (see page 12 of this prospectus);

Regulatory interpretation that classifies our hosting or related services as money transmission could impose additional compliance obligations, which could materially and adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations (see page 13 of this prospectus);

Increasing environmental regulations and carbon emission policies may increase our electricity costs and have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, and results of operations (see page 13 of this prospectus);

Changes in the tax treatment of digital assets could reduce market activity and demand for hosting services, which could materially and adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations (see page 13 of this prospectus); and
Our business is subject to complex and evolving laws and regulations regarding data protection (see page 14 of this prospectus).

There has been no public market for our common stock prior to this offering, and you may not be able to resell our common stock at or above the price you pay for them, or at all (see page 15 of this prospectus);

The market price of our common stock may be volatile or may decline regardless of our operating performance, and you may not be able to resell your shares of common stock at or above the initial public offering price (see page 15 of this prospectus);
You will experience immediate and substantial dilution in the net tangible book value of common stock purchased in this offering (see page 16 of this prospectus);

Our Certificate of Formation and Bylaws, as well as Texas law, contain provisions that could discourage acquisition bids or merger proposals, which may adversely affect the market price of our common stock and could deprive our investors of the opportunity to receive a premium for their shares (see page 16 of this prospectus);

If we fail to implement and maintain an effective system of internal controls, we may fail to meet our reporting obligations or be unable to accurately report our results of operations or prevent fraud, and investor confidence and the market price of our common stock may be materially and adversely affected (see page 17 of this prospectus);
We will incur substantial increased costs as a result of being a public company (see page 18 of this prospectus);
We may not be able to maintain the listing of our common stock on the Nasdaq Global Market (see page 19 of this prospectus);

Our management has broad discretion to determine how to use the funds raised in the offering and may use them in ways that may not enhance our results of operations or the price of our common stock (see page 19 of this prospectus); and

We will be a “controlled company” within the meaning of the Nasdaq listing rules and are allowed to follow certain exemptions from certain corporate governance requirements that could adversely affect our public stockholders (see page 20 of this prospectus).

notes.title: LEASES
text: On April 1, 2022, the Company obtained rights to use approximately two acres of land in Wheeler County, Texas for digital asset mining facilities through an assignment of easement rights from 913 Hero, LLC. The easement, originally entered into between 913 Hero, LLC and the landowners, has an initial term of ten years and requires annual consideration of $17,500, subject to adjustment for inflation and acreage.

On April 28, 2022, the Company entered into a related consulting agreement with 913 Hero, LLC, the original grantee of the easement, to facilitate the assignment and management of the easement rights. The consulting agreement has a 10-year term and requires monthly payments of $13,541.76, subject to adjustment based on electricity capacity and operating conditions. The Company is also responsible for all costs and obligations associated with the easement, including utilities, annual payments to the landowner, and applicable taxes. A security deposit equal to two months of consulting fees was paid upon execution.

notes.title: OPTION FEE FOR LAND PURCHASE
text: On November 4, 2024, the Company entered into a farm and ranch real estate purchase agreement to acquire a parcel of land located in Dumas, Texas, for a total purchase price of $80,000. In connection with the contract, the Company paid an option fee of $10,000 to the seller. The option grants the Company the right, but not the obligation, to purchase the property. The option fee will be applied to the purchase price if the transaction is completed. If the Company elects not to proceed, the option fee is non-refundable and will be retained by the seller.

The option expires on December 30, 2025. The Company expects to complete the transaction before the expiration date. As of reporting date, the option fee is recorded as a non-current asset on the Company’s consolidated balance sheets.

notes.title: TAXES
text: The Company is subjected to federal taxation in the United States, which is calculated in accordance with the Internal Revenue Code at the enacted statutory rate of 21% for the fiscal year ended July 31, 2025 and 2024. The Company is also subjected to Texas franchise tax (“margin tax”), which is legally characterized as a state income tax. The Texas franchise tax is imposed at a statutory rate of 0.75% of the Company’s taxable margin (defined generally as total revenue less certain deductions), rather than as a direct tax on net income. In accordance with ASC 740, the Texas franchise tax is treated as an income tax because it is based, in part, on income. Accordingly, the Company includes Texas franchise tax in its provision for income taxes.

notes.title: STOCKHOLDERS’ EQUITY
text: The Company was established under the laws of the State of Texas on April 19, 2022. At inception, the Company was authorized to issue 10,000 shares of common stock, with a par value of $0.001 per share, all of which were issued and outstanding.
Common Stock reclassification

On November 3, 2025, the Board of Directors and stockholders of the Company approved an amendment to the Company’s Certificate of Formation to (i) create two new classes of common stock, designated as Class A common stock and Class B common stock, which have equal economic rights, including equal rights to dividends and distributions, but unequal voting rights, and (ii) reclassify all issued and outstanding shares of common stock into shares of Class B common stock. Each Class A common stock entitles the holder to one vote per share, and each Class B common stock entitles the holder to 15 votes per share.

text: For the fiscal years ended July 31, 2025 and 2024, the Company had no stock options, warrants, or other potentially dilutive securities outstanding. As a result, basic and diluted earnings per share are the same.

Accordingly, the Company has determined that it operates as a single operating and reportable segment.
